subject: Clarify per-token metrics and commit tiers for Helix Health RFP
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: 2026-12-01T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify metrics for RFP - streaming tokens and rounding

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helix Health is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Our procurement team is finalizing the RFP responses and we need a clear, contract-ready description of how you measure 'billable tokens' versus streaming tokens, and how rounding/truncation is handled for streaming sessions. Specific asks: 

- For streaming responses (server-sent tokens), do you meter per-token, per-chunk, or per-second?
- If a streaming session produces partial tokens at billing window boundaries, do you round up/down or prorate?
- For committed-usage discounts, do committed volumes apply to gross tokens or to net billable tokens after rounding?

We have an internal target commit band we can share once we confirm the measurement definition. Can you provide a one-paragraph definition and a short example (numbers) we can paste into the RFP?

Best,
Alyssa Chen
VP, Product Integrations
Helix Health

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metrics for RFP - streaming tokens and rounding

Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: streaming output is billed as billable tokens, with a deterministic rounding policy applied at the per-request level before aggregation toward commit tiers. Below is a compact definition and a worked example you can use in the RFP. Attaching a concise metric appendix that we include in contracts (redwood-metric-appendix.pdf).

Definition (one-paragraph for RFP):
Redwood bills per token emitted by the model ("billable tokens"). For streaming responses, each streaming message is counted at the token boundary nearest to the emission; any partial token at the moment of emission is rounded up to the next whole token for billing. Billing is computed per request (stream session) and then aggregated across the billing window to determine commit utilization and overage. Streaming latency and byte-chunk boundaries do not alter token accounting — tokens are counted per model tokenizer output.

Illustrative example (RFP-ready):
- Single streaming response emits 102.4 tokenizer units during the lifetime of the request. Per-request rounding rule rounds this to 103 billable tokens.
- If a customer has a monthly commit of 1,000,000 tokens, that 103 counts toward the commit aggregate. Aggregation is applied after per-request rounding.

Notes / follow-ups:
- We can offer an alternative contract clause that bills streaming sessions by millisecond prorate if you need sub-token granularity for accounting, but this is uncommon and typically complicates billing reconciliation.
- Attached: redwood-metric-appendix.pdf (pulls these lines into contract-friendly language).

Suggested next step: quick call with procurement and our legal to walk the contract text. When are you available this week?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixhealth.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-02T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metrics for RFP - streaming tokens and rounding

Alyssa — adding a slightly more technical note for your engineers / procurement folks so there are no surprises. Quoting Dylan's paragraph above.

Technical note: tokens are counted after tokenization by the model's canonical tokenizer (we surface tokenizer version in the contract appendix). For streaming, we treat the output as a sequence of token emissions; if an emission corresponds to a partial token because the model is mid-token at an IO flush boundary, we round up that emission to the next whole token for billing. We do not attempt to stitch or prorate partial tokens across multiple emissions — billing is evaluated per request.

Contract clause snippet (suggested):
"Billable tokens" means the count of full tokens produced by the model's canonical tokenizer, with per-request rounding: any partial token produced during a request shall be rounded up to the nearest whole token prior to aggregation. Usage subject to commit tiers shall be calculated on aggregated per-request rounded token counts.

This approach keeps invoices deterministic and reconciliable. Happy to include the tokenizer version and a sample CSV export of token counts for your billing team.

—Monica
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixhealth.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-04T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metrics for RFP - streaming tokens and rounding (discount tiers / commit mapping)

Alyssa — adding the pricing side and practical commit mapping. High level: committed volume discounts are applied to aggregated billable tokens (post per-request rounding). We recommend committing to an expected gross token band; discounts then apply to the billed token volume after rounding. Some specifics you can include in the commercial appendix: 

- Commit bands (monthly): 250k–1M tokens: 7% off list; 1M–5M: 13% off; 5M–20M: 20% off; 20M+: custom enterprise pricing.
- Overage: billed at list price for any usage above the commit in the month, with a 30-day true-up window and option to convert overage to committed volume for future months.
- Rounding / reconciliation: bills show both raw token counts and post-rounding billed tokens; reconciliation CSV available on request.
- Streaming edge-case: if >50% of monthly tokens are streaming and your operations require millisecond-level accuracy for billing, we can add an alternative clause to bill streaming by 100ms granularity with prorated micro-charges (this requires an additional tracking flag and is billable as an add-on).

Contract language suggestion (commercial appendix):
The Provider shall meter "billable tokens" as defined in Appendix A. Committed volumes shall be applied against the aggregate of per-request rounded billable tokens. Discounts for committed tiers are applied to billed tokens. Overage is billed at list price and subject to a 30-day reconciliation and true-up.

Please note I CC'd Lauren from Legal to help with precise contract wording if you want the clause baked into the Master Services Agreement.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(attachment: redwood-metric-appendix.pdf)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: 2026-12-06T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify metrics for RFP - streaming tokens and rounding (discount tiers / commit mapping)

Thanks — this is helpful. A few notes from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement wants the streaming rounding softened to 100ms prorated increments rather than always rounding up at per-request boundary. Their concern is that long-running streams with many small flushes could inflate billed tokens. Is the 100ms billable add-on you called out something we can include in the base deal for the sizes in your 1M–5M band?
- Can you confirm that committed discounts apply after rounding (i.e., as you wrote) and that we would see both raw and billed counts on the invoice CSV? We need that during reconciliation with our internal chargeback.
- Also, we are asking for a one-time good-faith credit for any rounding delta in the first month after go-live (limited to 2% of the committed volume) — is that acceptable?

If you can confirm these points and share the updated SOW with the metric appendix merged, we can move the RFP to the final approval queue.

Best,
Alyssa

Subject: Re: Clarify metrics for RFP - streaming tokens and rounding (confirm next steps)

Alyssa — appreciate the clear asks. Quick responses and next steps below.

1) 100ms streaming granularity: we can accommodate this as the default for your account at the 1M–5M tier as a commercial concession. It will be implemented as an alternate billing mode for streaming: events aggregated into 100ms windows are prorated and then tokenized; per-window partial tokens are prorated rather than always rounded up. Note: this requires enabling the streaming-prorate flag on your account (ops change) and will add a small reconciliation field in the invoice CSV.

2) Commit discount application: confirmed — discounts apply after per-request rounding (post-rounding billed tokens). We will provide both raw tokenizer counts and billed token counts in the monthly CSV export and in the Console billing UI.

3) One-time good-faith credit: agreed — Redwood will provide a one-time credit up to 2% of the first-month committed volume to offset rounding deltas. We'll reflect this as a line-item credit in month one.

Next steps: 
- I've attached an updated SOW that merges the metric appendix and commercial appendix (SOW_v3.pdf).
- Lauren (Legal) will draft the precise MSA amendment language reflecting the streaming-prorate option and the one-time credit — Lauren, can you draft and share a redline by EOD Thursday?
- Aditya / Monica, please confirm implementation ETA for the streaming-prorate flag and the CSV field.
- Proposed call: Thursday 2026-12-09 10:00 AM PT to finalize. Alyssa, does that work?
